references.text: The preceding verse, [ref:Joh 3:16|John 3:16], explains the motivation behind God's sending of the Son: "For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son." Verse 17 expands on this by clarifying that the purpose was not judgment, but salvation.

In [ref:Joh 12:47|John 12:47], Jesus himself says: "I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world." This is an almost word-for-word parallel to John 3:17 and confirms that Jesus' mission in his first coming was salvation, not judgment.

In [ref:Joh 5:24|John 5:24], Jesus says that whoever hears his word and believes has eternal life and will not come under judgment. This expands on how the salvation described in John 3:17 is received through faith.
In [ref:1 Joh 4:14|1 John 4:14], John testifies: "The Father has sent the Son as the Savior of the world." This summarizes the message of John 3:17, that God sent the Son to save the world.

In [ref:Luk 9:56|Luke 9:56], Jesus says that the Son of Man has not come to destroy people's lives, but to save them. Note that this verse is textually disputed, but its content reflects the teaching in John 3:17 that the Son was not sent to judge, but to save.
In [ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10], Jesus says: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." The purpose of Jesus' coming—salvation, not judgment—aligns with the message of John 3:17.
Paul writes in [ref:1 Tim 1:15|1 Timothy 1:15]: "Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners." This confirms the central message of John 3:17 that God's purpose in sending the Son was salvation.

In [ref:Joh 8:15-16|John 8:15–16], Jesus says: "I do not judge anyone," but adds that if he does judge, his judgment is just. This nuances John 3:17 by showing that while Jesus has the authority to judge, his primary mission was not judgment.

In [ref:Jes 49:6|Isaiah 49:6], the Lord says that his servant shall be a light for the nations, so that his salvation may reach to the ends of the earth. This prophecy points to the universal purpose of salvation described in John 3:17—that the world should be saved through the Son.
In [ref:Joh 4:42|John 4:42], the Samaritans confess that Jesus is "the Savior of the world." This confirms that the Son was sent to save the whole world, as John 3:17 teaches.

In [ref:2 Kor 5:19|2 Corinthians 5:19], Paul writes that "God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them." This expands on John 3:17 by showing that God's purpose in sending Christ was reconciliation and salvation, not judgment.
